'''Jacob Everse Pullen''' (born November 10, 1989) is an American-Georgian professional [[basketball]] player for [[Napoli Basket (2016)|Napoli]] of the Italian [[Lega Basket Serie A]] (LBA). He played for the [[Kansas State Wildcats men's basketball|Kansas State Wildcats]].<ref>{{cite web|url=https://www.espn.com/nba/player/_/id/2282622/jacob-pullen |title=Player page |publisher=[[ESPN]] |access-date=March 22, 2010}}</ref> Pullen has both American and Georgian citizenship, and has played for the [[Georgia national basketball team|Georgian national team]].<ref name=":0" />

==College career==
In his college debut against Sacramento State, Pullen scored 18 points on 7-of-11 shooting and ended up scoring in double figures in eight of his first 10 games. He was a large part of Kansas State's renewed basketball success. As a freshman, he was one of just three players who appeared in all 33 games. Alongside [[Michael Beasley]], he helped upset #2 [[Kansas Jayhawks basketball|Kansas]] with a season-high 20 points, going 10-for-10 from the free throw line.{{citation needed|date=May 2023}}

In the 2008–09 season, Pullen was one of only two players to start all 34 games for the Wildcats (Luis Colon was the other). He notched his career best of 38 points against Kansas on Feb. 14, 2011. He recorded at least one steal in 27 games of the 2009 season and had at least one three-pointer in 29 games.<ref>{{cite web|url=http://collegebasketball.rivals.com/bviewplayer.asp?Player=83919#stats |title=Stats page |publisher=Collegebasketball.rivals.com |access-date=March 22, 2010}}</ref>

In the 2009–10 season, Pullen continued his strong play in his junior season, leading Kansas State to a 29–8 overall record (11–5, Big 12), with wins at Dayton, at UNLV, at Alabama, against Xavier, and against then undefeated, #1-ranked Texas. Playing under coach [[Frank Martin (basketball)|Frank Martin]], Pullen averaged 19.3 points per game on 41.9% shooting.<ref>{{cite web|url=https://www.kstatesports.com/roster.aspx?rp_id=3476|title=Jacob Pullen - Men's Basketball|publisher=[[Kansas State University]]|accessdate=April 5, 2022|url-status=live|archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20191115071505/https://www.kstatesports.com/sports/mens-basketball/roster/jacob-pullen/3476|archive-date=November 15, 2019}}</ref> With backcourt mate [[Denis Clemente]], Pullen received accolades for his part in the turnaround in K-State's basketball. In 2009–2010, Pullen and Clemente combined for the third-highest points-per-game of any guard tandem in school history, at almost 35 combined points. They trailed only the combo of Mike Evans and Chuckie Williams (who averaged more in both the 1974–75, and 1975–76 seasons) in the K-State record books. The two led the Wildcats to the Elite Eight of the NCAA Tournament before eventually losing to Butler. Pullen was selected to the  All Big-12 Team that year.<ref>[http://www.wibw.com/sports/headlines/81987577.html "Cats Guards Form Dangerous Duo"] {{Webarchive|url=https://web.archive.org/web/20110718043023/http://www.wibw.com/sports/headlines/81987577.html |date=July 18, 2011 }}, wibw.com, January 18, 2010. Retrieved January 19, 2010.</ref> As a senior, Pullen and the Cats lost to Wisconsin in the third round of the NCAA tournament and he was named a Fourth Team All-American by [[Fox Sports (United States)|Fox Sports]].<ref>{{cite news|first=Jeff |last=Goodman |url=http://msn.foxsports.com/collegebasketball/story/duke-blue-devils-notre-dame-fighting-irish-represented-postseason-honors-030711 |title=Goodman's 2010-11 All-America teams |work=[[Fox Sports (United States)|Fox Sports]] |publisher=Fox Sports Interactive Media |date=Mar 7, 2011 |access-date=June 21, 2011 |url-status=dead |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20140201123808/http://msn.foxsports.com/collegebasketball/story/duke-blue-devils-notre-dame-fighting-irish-represented-postseason-honors-030711 |archive-date=February 1, 2014 }}</ref> Pullen is the All Time Scoring Leader in the history of Kansas State University Men's Basketball with 2,132 career points.{{citation needed|date=May 2023}}

==Professional career==
===2011–12 season===
Pullen went undrafted in the [[2011 NBA draft]]. On July 12, 2011, he signed with [[Angelico Biella]] of the Italian [[Lega Basket Serie A]] for the 2011–12 season.<ref>{{cite news|title=Angelico Biella announces rookie Jacob Pullen|url=http://www.sportando.com/en/cat/nba/87270/angelico-biella-announces-rookie-jacob-pullen.html|access-date=September 28, 2014|work=Sportando.com|date=July 12, 2011}}</ref>

=== 2012–13 season===
In July 2012, Pullen joined the [[Philadelphia 76ers]] for the [[2012 NBA Summer League]].<ref>{{cite news|title=2012 76ers Summer League Team|url=http://www.nba.com/summer-league/2012/teams/sixers/|access-date=September 28, 2014|work=NBA.com}}</ref> On August 31, 2012, he signed with [[Hapoel Jerusalem B.C.|Hapoel Jerusalem]] of the [[Israeli Basketball Super League]] for the 2012–13 season.<ref>{{cite news|title=HAPOEL JERUSALEM adds promising Pullen|url=http://www.eurocupbasketball.com/eurocup/news/i/99448/hapoel-jerusalem-adds-promising-pullen|archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20150216182049/http://www.eurocupbasketball.com/eurocup/news/i/99448/hapoel-jerusalem-adds-promising-pullen|url-status=dead|archive-date=February 16, 2015|access-date=September 28, 2014|work=Eurocupbasketball.com|date=August 31, 2012}}</ref> On March 13, 2013, he signed with [[Virtus Pallacanestro Bologna|Virtus Bologna]] of Italy for the rest of the season.<ref>{{cite web| title =Virtus Bologna officially signs Jacob Pullen | publisher = Sportando.net | date =March 13, 2013| url =http://www.sportando.net/eng/italy/serie-a/52465/virtus-bologna-officially-signs-jacob-pullen.html | access-date = April 27, 2013}}</ref>

===2013–14 season===
On August 13, 2013, Pullen signed with [[FC Barcelona Bàsquet|FC Barcelona]] of Spain for the 2013–14 season.<ref>{{cite news|title=FC BARCELONA announces Jacob Pullen |url=http://www.euroleague.net/euroleaguenews/transactions/2013-14-signings/i/115365/8177/fc-barcelona-announces-jacob-pullen |access-date=September 28, 2014 |work=Euroleague.net |date=August 13, 2013 |url-status=dead |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20130825070729/http://www.euroleague.net/euroleaguenews/transactions/2013-14-signings/i/115365/8177/fc-barcelona-announces-jacob-pullen |archive-date=August 25, 2013 }}</ref> On 8 March 2014, Pullen scored 12 [[three-point field goal]]s in a 111–66 win over [[CB Valladolid]], breaking the [[Liga ACB]] single-game record, which was previously held by [[Oscar Schmidt]].<ref>{{cite web|url=http://www.acb.com/redaccion.php?id=101985|title=Jacob Pullen rompe el récord histórico de Oscar Schmidt|publisher=ACB.com|date=8 March 2014|language=es|access-date=10 March 2014|archive-date=30 June 2014|archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20140630123414/http://www.acb.com/redaccion.php?id=101985|url-status=dead}}</ref>

===2014–15 season===
In August 2014, he signed with [[Liaoning Flying Leopards]] of the [[Chinese Basketball Association]].<ref>{{cite news|title=Jacob Pullen leaves Barcelona to sign in China with Liaoning|url=http://www.sportando.com/en/world/asia/131217/jacob-pullen-leaves-barcelona-to-sign-in-china-with-liaoning.html|access-date=August 12, 2014|work=Sportando.com}}</ref> However, he left Liaoning before the start of the season. On September 28, 2014, Pullen returned to Spain and signed with [[CB Sevilla|Baloncesto Sevilla]].<ref>{{cite news|title=Baloncesto Sevilla officially lands Jacob Pullen|url=http://www.sportando.com/en/europe/spain/136049/baloncesto-sevilla-officially-lands-jacob-pullen.html|access-date=September 28, 2014|work=Sportando.com|date=September 28, 2014}}</ref> On November 7, 2014, he parted ways with Sevilla.<ref>{{cite news|title=Baloncesto Sevilla parts ways with Jacob Pullen|url=http://www.sportando.com/en/europe/spain/140351/baloncesto-sevilla-parts-ways-with-jacob-pullen.html|access-date=November 7, 2014|work=Sportando.com|date=November 7, 2014}}</ref>

On November 14, 2014, he signed with [[New Basket Brindisi]] of Italy for the rest of the season.<ref>{{cite news|title=Enel Brindisi announces Jacob Pullen|url=http://www.sportando.com/en/italy/serie-a/141105/enel-brindisi-announces-jacob-pullen.html|access-date=November 14, 2014|work=Sportando.com|date=November 14, 2014}}</ref>

===2015–16 season===
On August 8, 2015, Pullen signed with [[KK Cedevita|Cedevita Zagreb]] of Croatia for the 2015–16 season.<ref>{{cite news|title=Potpisao playmaker Jacob Pullen|url=http://www.kkcedevita.hr/vijesti/tabid/86/id/34068/potpisao-playmaker-jacob-pullen.aspx#.VcXyTbVi5uE|access-date=August 8, 2015|work=kkcedevita.hr|date=August 8, 2015|language=hr}}</ref>

===2016–17 season===
On September 29, 2016, Pullen signed a one-month deal with Russian club [[BC Khimki|Khimki]].<ref>{{cite news|title=BC Khimki adds in guard Pullen|url=http://en.bckhimki.ru/news/clubnews/2016/september/1130/|access-date=September 29, 2016|work=bckhimki.ru|date=September 29, 2016}}</ref> On October 31, he re-signed with Khimki for the rest of the season.<ref>{{cite news|title=Khimki Moscow keeps Jacob Pullen for the season|url=http://www.sportando.com/en/europe/russia/215977/khimki-moscow-keeps-jacob-pullen-for-the-season.html|access-date=October 31, 2016|work=Sportando.com|date=October 31, 2016}}</ref> He was officially released from the Russian team on July 4, 2017.

===2017–18 season===
On September 22, 2017, Pullen signed with the [[Philadelphia 76ers]].<ref>{{cite web|title=Sixers Sign Jacob Pullen|url=http://www.nba.com/sixers/news/sixers-sign-jacob-pullen|website=NBA.com|access-date=September 22, 2017|date=September 22, 2017}}</ref> On October 14, his contract was converted to a [[Two-way contract|two-way deal]]. Under terms of the deal, he split time between the 76ers and their [[NBA G League|G League]] affiliate, the [[Delaware Blue Coats|Delaware 87ers]].<ref>{{cite web|title=Jacob Pullen's Contract Converted To Two-Way Deal|url=http://www.nba.com/sixers/news/philadelphia-76ers-convert-jacob-pullens-contract-two-way-deal|website=NBA.com|access-date=October 14, 2017|date=October 14, 2017}}</ref> On January 4, 2018, he was waived by the 76ers after appearing in three NBA games.<ref>{{cite news|title=Philadelphia 76ers waive Jacob Pullen|url=http://www.nba.com/article/2018/01/04/sixers-waive-two-way-player-jacob-pullen/#/|access-date=January 5, 2018|work=NBA.com|date=January 4, 2018}}</ref>

On January 7, 2018, Pullen signed with [[Mahram Tehran BC|Mahram Tehran]] of the [[Iranian Basketball Super League|Iranian Super League]] for the rest of the season.<ref>{{cite news|title=Jacob Pullen signs in Iran with Mahram|url=http://archive.sportando.basketball/it/asia/iran/260273/jacob-pullen-signs-in-iran-with-mahram.html|access-date=July 28, 2019|work=Sportando.com|date=January 7, 2018}}</ref>

On February 20, 2018, Pullen signed with [[Afyon Belediye S.K.|Afyon Belediye]] of the Turkish second-tier [[Turkish Basketball First League]] (TBL).<ref>{{cite news|title=Jacob Pullen signs with Afyon Belediyespor|url=http://archive.sportando.basketball/it/turkey/tbl/265423/jacob-pullen-signs-with-afyon-belediyespor.html|access-date=July 28, 2019|work=Sportando.com|date=February 20, 2018}}</ref> With Afyon, he won promotion to the first-tier [[Basketbol Süper Ligi]] (BSL) after winning the play-off finals.<ref>{{Cite web|url=https://www.cnnturk.com/spor/basketbol/afyonda-cifte-sevinc-afyon-belediyespor-basketbol-super-liginde|title=Afyon'da çifte sevinç: Afyon Belediyespor Basketbol Süper Ligi'nde|date=1 June 2018|access-date=1 June 2018|language=tr|publisher=[[CNN Türk]]}}</ref>

===2018–19 season===
On November 1, 2018, Pullen returned to [[KK Cedevita|Cedevita Zagreb]] for his second stint with the club.<ref>{{cite news|title=Cedevita brings back Jacob Pullen|url=https://www.eurocupbasketball.com/eurocup/news/i/98bse4k6yty7fnig/cedevita-brings-back-jacob-pullen|archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20181126184050/http://www.eurocupbasketball.com/eurocup/news/i/98bse4k6yty7fnig/cedevita-brings-back-jacob-pullen|url-status=dead|archive-date=November 26, 2018|access-date=July 28, 2019|work=Eurocupbasketball.com|date=November 1, 2018}}</ref>

===Mornar (2019–2021)===
On July 12, 2019, Pullen signed with Montenegrin club [[KK Mornar Bar|Mornar Bar]] of the [[ABA League]].<ref>{{cite news|title=Mornar Bar inks Jacob Pullen|url=https://sportando.basketball/en/mornar-bar-inks-jacob-pullen/|access-date=July 28, 2019|work=Sportando.com|date=July 12, 2019}}</ref>

Pullen averaged 16 points, three assists, and 1.4 assists per game during the 2020–21 season with Mornar Bar.<ref name="yahyabeyoglu" />

===2021–22 season===
On August 9, 2021, Pullen signed with [[KK Cedevita Olimpija]] of the [[Premier A Slovenian Basketball League|Slovenian Basketball League]].<ref name="yahyabeyoglu">{{cite web |last1=Yahyabeyoglu |first1=Fersu |title=Jacob Pullen (ex Mornar) joins KK Cedevita Olimpija Ljubljana |url=https://www.eurobasket.com/Eurocup/news/698937/Jacob-Pullen-(ex-Mornar)-joins-KK-Cedevita-Olimpija-Ljubljana |website=Eurobasket |access-date=August 9, 2021 |date=August 9, 2021}}</ref>

===2023–24 season===
On August 26, 2023, he signed with [[Napoli Basket (2016)|Napoli Basket]] of the Italian [[Lega Basket Serie A]] (LBA).<ref>{{Cite news|url=https://sportando.basketball/en/gevi-napoli-lands-jacob-pullen/|title=GeVi Napoli lands Jacob Pullen|last=|first=|date=August 26, 2023|website=|newspaper=Sportando|language=En|access-date=September 3, 2023 |last1=Borghesan |first1=Ennio Terrasi }}</ref>

===2025–26 season===
On November 28, 2025, he signed with [[Dinamo Sassari]] of the Italian [[Lega Basket Serie A]] (LBA).<ref>{{Cite web|url=https://www.dinamobasket.com/blog/il-talento-di-jacob-pullen-al-servizio-della-dinamo|title=Il talento di Jacob Pullen al servizio della Dinamo|last=|first=|date=November 28, 2025|website=dinamobasket.com|publisher=|language=it|access-date=November 30, 2025}}</ref>

==National team career==
In August, 2012, Pullen was granted Georgian citizenship, which increased his career options across Europe and allowed him to play for the [[Georgian national basketball team|Georgian national team]] in [[FIBA EuroBasket 2013|EuroBasket 2013]].<ref name=":0">{{cite web| title =Jacob Pullen Granted Georgian Citizenship, Will Play As Bosman | publisher = RealGM.com| date =August 7, 2012| url =http://basketball.realgm.com/wiretap/222845/Jacob_Pullen_Granted_Georgian_Citizenship_Will_Play_As_Bosman | access-date = August 31, 2012}}</ref>  He began playing with the team during [[FIBA EuroBasket 2013 qualification|EuroBasket qualification]] in 2012.{{citation needed|date=May 2023}}
